input_signals.name: Profitable Hiring Restraint
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, emp)), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(emp, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating profit per employee and restrained employee growth earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: High profit per employee combined with limited hiring suggests scalable profitability and operating discipline. In contrast, profitable firms expanding headcount aggressively may be investing ahead of realized demand, increasing the risk of future margin disappointment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, emp ) ), ind_rank( neg( growth( emp, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capacity Growth Profit Productivity Fade
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppent, 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, ppent), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms expanding physical capacity while operating profit per unit of PPE is deteriorating earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal targets aggressive investment only when it is accompanied by declining productivity of the invested asset base. This avoids simply shorting all profitable growers and instead isolates cases where expansion appears to be weakening marginal returns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( growth( ppent, 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( oibdp, ppent ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Lean Inventory Margin Expansion
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with improving operating margins while inventory intensity declines earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Margin expansion is more credible when it occurs without inventory buildup, because it is less likely to reflect overproduction, channel stuffing, or unsold stock accumulation. The signal pairs profitability improvement with working-capital discipline rather than treating either effect in isolation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( delta( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( invt, sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Margin Inventory Efficiency
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(invt, sale))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high gross margins and low inventory intensity earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts away from PPE-growth variants and focuses on inventory capital productivity. A firm that earns strong gross profitability without tying up much balance-sheet investment in inventory is a disciplined cash generator, while high-margin firms requiring heavy inventory investment may have less attractive true economics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( invt, sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hiring Pause Margin Leverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(emp, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms expanding operating margins without expanding headcount earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests operating leverage from labor discipline rather than the lower-coverage level effect of profit per employee. Margin gains achieved without aggressive hiring suggest scalable profitability and disciplined investment in labor capacity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( growth( emp, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Durability Inventory Stability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3))), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(invt, sale), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high and stable operating margins plus stable inventory intensity earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the gross-margin-change and inventory-change clone with a durability mechanism: profitability is more valuable when it is not accompanied by unstable working-capital requirements. The MIN structure requires all three traits, so the high-score tail is not reached by profitability alone or by a standalone inventory signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( invt, sale ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitable Inventory Intensity Deceleration
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, sale)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High-margin firms whose inventory intensity is decelerating earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the prior dimensional mismatch by evaluating the change-of-change in inventory intensity itself rather than subtracting unlike quantities. The economic mechanism is that profitable firms become more attractive when the pace of working-capital absorption slows, suggesting better inventory discipline without simply repeating a one-year inventory-drawdown signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( accel( ratio( invt, sale ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Deleveraging Profit Harvest
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(xint, sale), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-profitable firms that reduce leverage and lower interest burden earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal targets firms using cash generation to improve capital discipline rather than to fund aggressive expansion. Requiring both debt reduction and falling interest intensity makes the mechanism more specific than a standalone profitability or issuance effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( xint, sale ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Prior Operating Capital Payoff
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(LAG(GROWTH(ADD(ppent, invt), 1), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(ppent, invt)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms whose prior tangible operating-capital expansion is followed by improving profit per dollar of plant and inventory earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This no longer rewards firms for having little invested capital or for a single return-on-capital ratio. The high-score tail requires an actual prior investment expansion, a profitable operating state, and evidence that the added operating capital is converting into better productivity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( lag( growth( add( ppent, invt ), 1 ), 1 ) ), min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, add( ppent, invt ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Expensed RND Intangible Restraint
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(intan, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that remain profitable while expensing R&D and avoiding capitalized intangible buildup earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Profitability is more impressive when it survives expensed innovation spending rather than being supported by capitalized intangible investment. Treating missing R&D as zero is economically natural, while the high-score tail still requires actual R&D intensity, current profitability, and intangible-asset restraint.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( intan, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Retained as Liquidity

input_signals.hypothesis: High-gross-margin firms shifting balance-sheet resources toward cash rather than physical expansion earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the prior inventory-efficiency duplicate by measuring capital-allocation mix: whether profitable product economics are being retained as liquidity instead of absorbed by plant expansion. The mechanism is disciplined harvesting and optionality among profitable firms, not a standalone gross-margin or inventory anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sub( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ), delta( ratio( ppent, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cumulative RND Harvest No Capitalization
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(sale, 5))), MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(intan, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial historical expensed R&D, improving operating margins, and restrained capitalized intangible growth earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether past expensed innovation is now converting into profits without requiring balance-sheet intangible buildup. It extends the R&D-intangible discipline theme from current spending to cumulative innovation investment and realized margin payoff.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), ts_sum( sale, 5 ) ) ), min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( intan, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitable Capex Inventory Rotation
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms increasing capex while reducing inventory intensity earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not another capex-restraint signal; it tests whether profitable firms can fund or accompany fixed-capital investment with working-capital release. The interaction treats investment as disciplined when it is paired with inventory efficiency, rather than assuming all investment increases are value destroying.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( invt, sale ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RND Product Margin Inventory Release
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(sale, 5))), MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial cumulative expensed R&D whose gross margins improve while inventory intensity falls earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal asks whether past innovation spending is translating into product-level pricing power without requiring more inventory capital. This combines the strong R&D-harvest theme with a concrete operating-capital discipline test rather than simply rewarding low investment.

input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), ts_sum( sale, 5 ) ) ), min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( invt, sale ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fresh Plant Harvest Margin
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ppegt, ppent))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with relatively fresh physical assets, declining capex intensity, and improving after-depreciation operating margins earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This targets firms exiting an investment cycle after renewing their asset base, not firms merely cutting capex because assets are old. Improving after-depreciation margins suggest the refreshed plant is now producing an economic payoff while reinvestment needs are easing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( ppegt, ppent ) ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deleveraging With Maintenance Discipline

input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-profitable firms that reduce debt while keeping capex close to depreciation earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This improves on simple cash-profitable deleveraging by requiring that debt reduction is not achieved through obvious capex starvation or aggressive overinvestment. Capex near depreciation indicates maintenance discipline, making the cash generation more sustainable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( abs( ratio( sub( capx, dp ), at ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial cumulative expensed R&D whose operating margins and sales per tangible operating asset are improving earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the redundant R&D-count gate and does not simply swap accounting-margin improvement for cash-margin improvement in the prior R&D signal. The mechanism is commercialization efficiency: past expensed innovation is valuable when it produces both better margins and better utilization of plant-plus-inventory capital.

input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), ts_sum( sale, 5 ) ) ), min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( sale, add( ppent, invt ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deleveraging Replacement Capex Balance
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), ADD(capx, dp)))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-profitable firms reducing debt while keeping capex close to depreciation earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the maintenance-discipline idea by measuring capex balance relative to depreciation directly, rather than favoring asset-light firms with tiny capex and depreciation. The signal rewards firms that generate cash, delever, and maintain the asset base without either starving or aggressively expanding it.

input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms with aged physical assets but balanced replacement capex earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The aged-asset underinvestment evidence suggests that low capex is dangerous when the asset base is old.
